hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 学生; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: Student introductions and birthday conversations both use 生. Its five-stroke shape is also a useful comparison with the simpler 牛.

components.explanation: A short upper slant leads into three horizontals joined by a central vertical. The lowest horizontal supports the whole form.

readingNotes: Read 生 as shēng with a level first tone in 生日 (shēngrì) and 生活 (shēnghuó). In 学生, the final syllable is often unstressed neutral sheng in conversation; the careful dictionary form is xuéshēng.
usage: 生 appears in 学生 for student, 生日 for birthday, and 生活 for life. These compounds express different ideas; 生 alone is not the usual word for a student.
writingTip: Keep the upper slant short, space the horizontal levels evenly, and let the bottom horizontal be wider than the middle one.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 他出生在中国，现在住在英国。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Tā chūshēng zài Zhōngguó, xiànzài zhù zài Yīngguó.
exampleSentences.meaning: He was born in China and now lives in Britain.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 生 has an extra bottom horizontal compared with 牛; omitting it changes the character.

seo.title: 生 (shēng) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 生 (shēng): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 生 (shēng), its five-stroke form, and its contrast with 牛. Practise student, birthday, and everyday-life words with useful sentences.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 老师; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: 老师 is one of the first words learners need in a classroom. Practise 老 as part of that respectful title before using it to describe age.

components.explanation: The upper part has a crossing horizontal and vertical with a falling stroke. A compact 匕-shaped form occupies the lower part.

readingNotes: 老 is lǎo, a third-tone syllable. In 老师 (lǎoshī) it precedes a first tone; in 老虎 (lǎohǔ), ordinary speech changes the first of the two third tones to a rising tone.
usage: 老 can describe age, but 老师 is the respectful everyday word for teacher, not an old teacher. 老朋友 describes a longtime friend and need not refer to an elderly person.
writingTip: Keep the upper crossing compact and leave room beneath the long falling stroke for the lower hooked form.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 我们虽然住得很远，但一直是老朋友。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒmen suīrán zhù de hěn yuǎn, dàn yìzhí shì lǎo péngyou.
exampleSentences.meaning: Although we live far apart, we have remained longtime friends.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 老 has 匕 at the bottom, while 考 has a different lower hook; compare the lower parts before copying.

seo.title: 老 (lǎo) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 老 (lǎo): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 老 (lǎo), distinguish it from 考, and learn why 老师 and 老朋友 do not simply mean old people. Includes tone and writing guidance.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 老师; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: Writing a teacher's title or describing an occupation often requires 师. Its small top-right horizontal is easy to miss when copying quickly.

components.explanation: Two narrow strokes stand on the left. On the right, a top horizontal covers a 巾-shaped form with a central vertical.

readingNotes: 师 is pronounced shī with a level first tone. Keep it distinct from 四 sì: shī has the retroflex sh initial rather than the plain s initial.
usage: 师 occurs in roles such as 老师, 教师, 医师 and 律师. It is normally part of a complete occupation word; 老师 is the usual way to address a teacher.
writingTip: Leave a gap between the narrow left strokes and the right component, and keep the long right vertical centred under its top horizontal.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 我想成为一名汉语教师。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chéngwéi yì míng Hànyǔ jiàoshī.
exampleSentences.meaning: I want to become a Chinese language teacher.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 师 includes a top horizontal on the right that 帅 does not have.

seo.title: 师 (shī) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 师 (shī): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 师 (shī) stroke order and its distinction from 帅. Practise 老师, 教师, and other occupation words with a clear sh pronunciation.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 同学; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: Use 同 to recognise shared connections between classmates and colleagues. The open outer frame makes it useful enclosure practice.

components.explanation: A broad 冂 surrounds a short horizontal and a small 口. The outer frame remains open at the bottom.

readingNotes: 同 has the rising second tone tóng. It keeps that reading in 同学 (tóngxué), 同事 (tóngshì), and 同意 (tóngyì).
usage: 同 contributes the idea of sharing or sameness. 同学 is a schoolmate, 同事 is a colleague, and 同意 means agree; these are not interchangeable person words.
writingTip: Make the outer frame tall enough to contain the short horizontal and small box without letting them touch its sides.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 我们来自不同的国家，却在同一个班学习。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒmen láizì bù tóng de guójiā, què zài tóng yí ge bān xuéxí.
exampleSentences.meaning: We come from different countries but study in the same class.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 同 has one short horizontal above its inner 口, while 周 has a more complex upper interior.

seo.title: 同 (tóng) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 同 (tóng): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 同 (tóng) with an open outer frame. Learn the differences between 同学, 同事, 同意, and 相同 through examples.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 朋友; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: 朋友 belongs in early introductions and social conversations. Writing 朋 helps learners notice two repeated shapes without merging their strokes.

components.explanation: Two 月-shaped components sit side by side, each with its own pair of inner horizontal lines.

readingNotes: 朋 is péng with a rising second tone. In 朋友, 友 is usually unstressed: péngyou. Avoid reading the second syllable as a strongly accented yǒu in ordinary conversation.
usage: 朋 is most useful to beginners inside 朋友. It does not usually stand alone as the everyday noun friend; 男朋友 and 女朋友 can mean boyfriend and girlfriend.
writingTip: Keep both 月 forms readable and leave a narrow gap between them; do not merge their middle horizontals into continuous lines.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 周末我想和朋友一起去爬山。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ xiǎng hé péngyou yìqǐ qù páshān.
exampleSentences.meaning: I want to go mountain climbing with friends this weekend.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 朋 has two 月-shaped parts, while 明 has 日 on the left and 月 on the right.

seo.title: 朋 (péng) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 朋 (péng): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 朋 (péng), its paired 月 shapes, and the pronunciation of 朋友. Practise friend and relationship words without confusing 朋 with 明.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 朋友; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: Friendship vocabulary links 友 to people and shared activities. Compare its lower form with 右 while practising words you can use with classmates.

components.explanation: A horizontal and long falling stroke sit above a 又-shaped lower part whose final strokes spread apart.

readingNotes: Use yǒu, a third tone, in 友好 (yǒuhǎo) and 友谊 (yǒuyì). In the common word 朋友, 友 usually becomes neutral you.
usage: 友 appears in words for friendship and shared activities. 友好 means friendly, 友谊 means friendship, and 队友 is a teammate rather than just any friend.
writingTip: Keep the upper falling stroke long enough to cover the lower 又, then let the final right fall balance the left side.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 我们毕业以后仍然保持着友谊。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒmen bìyè yǐhòu réngrán bǎochí zhe yǒuyì.
exampleSentences.meaning: We maintained our friendship after graduation.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 友 has 又 below its upper strokes, whereas 右 has 口 at the bottom.

seo.title: 友 (yǒu) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 友 (yǒu): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 友 (yǒu) and distinguish it from 右. Learn neutral you in 朋友 and compare friendship, friendliness, and teammate vocabulary.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 名字; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: Names are needed on worksheets, forms, and introductions. 名 also introduces a useful distinction between a name and a measure word for a person.

components.explanation: 夕 occupies the upper part and 口 sits below it. The box belongs below the falling shape rather than beside it.

readingNotes: 名 is míng with a rising second tone. It sounds the same as 明 in standard Mandarin, but 名字 and 明天 use different characters and meanings.
usage: 名字 is the everyday word for a name. 名 also appears in 有名 for famous and as a measure word for people in 一名学生; do not use 名字 for every occurrence of 名.
writingTip: Keep 夕 compact and centre the lower 口 beneath it, leaving a clear gap between the two parts.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ míngzi xiě zài zhèlǐ.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 这位老师在我们学校很有名。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎoshī zài wǒmen xuéxiào hěn yǒumíng.
exampleSentences.meaning: This teacher is well known at our school.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 名 has 夕 above 口, while 各 has 夂; inspect the upper strokes rather than only the lower box.

seo.title: 名 (míng) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 名 (míng): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 名 (míng), with 夕 above 口. Practise 名字, 有名, 名单, and 一名学生, including the person-classifier use.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 叫; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 我叫… is a practical first sentence for meeting someone. Learn to write 叫 and connect its falling tone with that introduction.

components.explanation: A small 口 stands beside 丩, a narrow turning form crossed by a longer vertical on the right.

readingNotes: 叫 is jiào with a falling fourth tone. Keep it distinct from 教 jiāo in 教汉语: the initial sounds are similar, but the tones differ.
usage: 叫 introduces a name in 我叫李明 and can also mean call out. 叫人 can mean call someone over; the words following 叫 determine the intended action.
writingTip: Keep 口 small and slightly high, and leave space before the long vertical of the right component.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào zài zhèlǐ dàjiào.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 你听见外面小鸟的叫声了吗？
exampleSentences.pinyin: Nǐ tīngjiàn wàimian xiǎoniǎo de jiàoshēng le ma?
exampleSentences.meaning: Did you hear the birds calling outside?

confusableCharacter.guidance: 叫 has 口 on the left, while 收 has a different left shape and 攵 on the right.

seo.title: 叫 (jiào) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 叫 (jiào): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 叫 (jiào) in five strokes. Learn how to introduce a name, call someone over, and distinguish jiào from the teaching verb jiāo.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 什么; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: 什么 lets beginners ask about unfamiliar objects and words. Learning 什 alongside 么 turns a four-stroke character into a useful question.

components.explanation: The person radical 亻 is narrow on the left and 十 forms a clear cross on the right.

readingNotes: Use shén in 什么 (shénme). The separate reading shí occurs in words such as 什锦 (shíjǐn, assorted); this guide's main reading is the question-word use.
usage: 什 normally occurs with 么 when asking what. 什么书 asks what book, 为什么 asks why, and 没什么 means nothing much; do not use 什 alone as the question word.
writingTip: Keep the person radical slim and the cross on the right lower than the top of the left falling stroke.

exampleSentences.meaning: What book would you like to read?
Why do you want to study Chinese?

confusableCharacter.guidance: 什 includes 亻 to the left of 十; dropping the radical changes the reading and meaning.

seo.title: 什 (shén) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 什 (shén): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 什 (shén), the first character of 什么. Compare shén with shí in 什锦 and practise what and why questions.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 什么; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: 么 appears at the end of several everyday questions. Its short written form and neutral pronunciation are both worth practising early.

components.explanation: A short falling stroke sits above a small open 厶-like lower turn and dot. The outline should not become a closed triangle.

readingNotes: 么 is normally neutral me in 什么 (shénme), 怎么 (zěnme), 这么 (zhème), and 那么 (nàme). Do not add a full lexical tone to the final syllable in these words.
usage: 么 completes several common question and degree words. 什么 asks what, 怎么 asks how, and 这么 or 那么 indicates a degree or manner; 么 is not normally used alone here.
writingTip: Keep the upper slant separate from the lower turn, and place the final dot so the lower shape remains open.

exampleSentences.meaning: How do you go to school?
Why is it so cold today?

exampleSentences.hanzi: 我不知道他为什么那么高兴。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhīdào tā wèishénme nàme gāoxìng.
exampleSentences.meaning: I do not know why he is so happy.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 么 has one upper slant, while 公 has two spreading upper strokes above 厶.

seo.title: 么 (me) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 么 (me): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 么 (me) in three strokes and keep its neutral tone. Distinguish 什么, 怎么, 这么, and 那么 with beginner questions.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 吗; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: A single 吗 can turn a statement into a yes-no question. Practise its written form while learning when the particle is unnecessary.

components.explanation: 口 forms the small left component, and 马 occupies the larger right side. The mouth radical is separate from the horse-shaped part.

readingNotes: Use neutral ma at the end of ordinary yes-no questions. The character has other dictionary readings, but the questions on this page use the unstressed particle.
usage: 吗 turns a statement into a yes-no question, as in 你是学生吗？ It is not normally added to a basic question that already uses 什么 or 谁 to request information.
writingTip: Keep 口 narrow and slightly high, and leave enough width for 马 on the right without joining their strokes.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 你现在可以和我一起去图书馆吗？
exampleSentences.pinyin: Nǐ xiànzài kěyǐ hé wǒ yìqǐ qù túshūguǎn ma?
exampleSentences.meaning: Can you go to the library with me now?

confusableCharacter.guidance: 吗 has 口 on the left; 妈 has 女. Both contain 马 but serve different words.

seo.title: 吗 (ma) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 吗 (ma): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 吗 (ma), the neutral-tone yes-no question particle. Compare 吗 with 妈 and practise questions without adding 吗 to ordinary what questions.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 呢; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 呢 helps learners keep a conversation going with short follow-up questions. Its role becomes clearer in a dialogue than in an isolated translation.

components.explanation: A small 口 stands beside 尼. The right component has a 尸-shaped cover above a compact lower hooked form.

readingNotes: Use neutral ne in 你呢？ and 在看书呢. The reading ní occurs in fabric words such as 呢子 (nízi); that is a separate use from the particle taught here.
usage: 呢 can ask a follow-up question when the topic is understood, as in 我很好，你呢？ It also adds emphasis to an ongoing state; it does not simply replace 吗 in every question.
writingTip: Keep 口 compact, give the upper 尸 on the right room to stretch downward, and keep the lower strokes inside its cover.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 我的书刚才还在这里，现在在哪儿呢？
exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒ de shū gāngcái hái zài zhèlǐ, xiànzài zài nǎr ne?
exampleSentences.meaning: My book was here just now; where is it now?

confusableCharacter.guidance: 呢 has 口 on the left, whereas 泥 has 氵; both share 尼 on the right.

seo.title: 呢 (ne) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 呢 (ne): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 呢 (ne) and learn follow-up questions such as 你呢？ Compare its neutral-tone particle use with 吗 and the separate fabric reading ní.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 很; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 很 often appears before adjectives in beginner sentences. Pair its writing practice with tone practice rather than treating it only as the English word very.

components.explanation: 彳 occupies the narrow left side, while 艮 forms the taller right part with a compact upper box and spreading lower finish.

readingNotes: 很 is hěn with a third tone. Before another third tone, as in 很好, the first syllable is pronounced with a rising tone in normal speech; written Pinyin usually retains hěn hǎo.
usage: 很 commonly precedes adjectives. In a simple sentence such as 我很好 it can provide a neutral link rather than strongly stressing very; the context and emphasis affect the translation.
writingTip: Keep 彳 narrow, leave the right box clear, and avoid crowding the lower strokes of 艮 into the left radical.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Zhè běn shū hěn yǒu yìsi.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 虽然这道题很难，我还是想试一试。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Suīrán zhè dào tí hěn nán, wǒ háishi xiǎng shì yi shì.
exampleSentences.meaning: Although this question is difficult, I still want to try.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 很 has 彳 on the left, while 狠 has 犭; the right component is the same.

seo.title: 很 (hěn) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 很 (hěn): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 很 (hěn), its contrast with 狠, and third-tone change in 很好. Practise degree expressions without translating every 很 as strongly stressed very.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 都; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 都 helps describe what classmates or family members have in common. Its position beside 不 can change whether a sentence means none or not all.

components.explanation: 者 forms the larger left component and 阝 forms a narrow right-side ear-like component. The two lower parts remain separated.

readingNotes: Use dōu, a first tone, for all or both. Use dū in 首都 (shǒudū, capital city) and 都市 (dūshì, city); these are different word senses.
usage: 都 normally comes after the subject and before the verb or adjective: 我们都去. 我们不都去 means not all of us go, while 我们都不去 means none of us go.
writingTip: Keep 者 wider than 阝 and avoid stretching the right radical to the full width of the left component.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Tāmen liǎng ge dōu xǐhuan hē chá.
exampleSentences.meaning: Both of them like drinking tea.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 这些书我不都喜欢，但每本都看过。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Zhèxiē shū wǒ bù dōu xǐhuan, dàn měi běn dōu kàn guo.
exampleSentences.meaning: I do not like all these books, but I have read each one.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 都 adds 阝 on the right of 者; omitting that radical leaves a different character.

seo.title: 都 (dōu) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 都 (dōu): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 都 (dōu), distinguish it from dū in 首都, and compare 都不 with 不都. Includes examples for all, both, and partial negation.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 2 vocabulary PDF includes 要; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: 要 is useful for requests, needs, and plans. Learning its contexts helps learners choose between a direct request and a softer expression with 想.

components.explanation: 覀 forms a compact upper cover above 女. The lower crossing strokes spread more widely than the interior of the upper component.

readingNotes: Read 要 as yào in 我要, 需要, and 重要. The reading yāo appears in words such as 要求 (yāoqiú, request or requirement); the common want/need use is fourth tone.
usage: 要 can express wanting, needing, or an approaching event. 我要水 is a direct request, while 我想喝水 is softer; 快要下雨了 means it is about to rain.
writingTip: Keep the upper cover shallow enough to leave room for 女 and its final horizontal, without letting the lower part lean to one side.

exampleSentences.meaning: I would like a glass of water.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 快要下雨了，我们需要带伞。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Kuàiyào xià yǔ le, wǒmen xūyào dài sǎn.
exampleSentences.meaning: It is about to rain; we need to take an umbrella.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 要 has 覀 above 女, while 耍 has 而 above 女; compare the upper component.

seo.title: 要 (yào) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 要 (yào): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 要 (yào) stroke order and its want, need, and approaching-event uses. Compare yào with yāo in 要求 and practise polite alternatives.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 会; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 会 helps learners describe a new skill, such as writing a character. It also appears in predictions and meeting vocabulary, so context matters.

components.explanation: 人 forms a broad upper cover above 云. The lower part contains two horizontals and an open turn with a dot.

readingNotes: Read 会 as huì in 会写, 开会, and 会议. In 会计 (kuàijì, accounting or accountant), the same character is kuài; do not carry huì into that word.
usage: 会 can express a learned skill or an expected event. 我会写汉字 describes a skill, while 明天会下雨 predicts rain. Compare 能 for ability or possibility under current conditions.
writingTip: Make the 人 cover broad and leave a gap above 云; keep the lower turn open rather than drawing a closed triangle.

exampleSentences.meaning: The teacher has a meeting this afternoon.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 多练习以后，你会说得更自然。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Duō liànxí yǐhòu, nǐ huì shuō de gèng zìrán.
exampleSentences.meaning: With more practice, you will speak more naturally.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 会 adds a 人-shaped cover above 云; the top component must not disappear.

seo.title: 会 (huì) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 会 (huì): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 会 (huì), learn skills versus predictions, and compare 会 with 能. Includes the separate kuài reading in 会计 and meeting vocabulary.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 能; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 能 is useful when asking for help or explaining what is possible today. Its form and meaning make a useful next step after learning 会.

components.explanation: The left part has 厶 above a 月-shaped form, while two 匕-shaped forms are stacked on the right.

readingNotes: 能 is néng with a rising second tone in 能力, 可能, and 能够. Keep the final ng sound; it differs from the n ending in words such as 您 nín.
usage: 能 expresses ability or possibility in the circumstances. 今天我不能去 can mean circumstances prevent going; 会 often describes a learned skill. Permission questions can also use 能.
writingTip: Keep the two right-hand hooked forms distinct, and avoid squeezing the left lower box until its inner lines touch.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 如果每天练习，你就能写得更好。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Rúguǒ měitiān liànxí, nǐ jiù néng xiě de gèng hǎo.
exampleSentences.meaning: If you practise every day, you can write better.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 能 appears above four dots in 熊; 能 alone has no bottom row of dots.

seo.title: 能 (néng) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 能 (néng): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 能 (néng), its stacked right-hand forms, and the difference from 熊. Compare 能 with 会 using ability and possibility examples.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 想; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 想 connects personal wishes, ideas, and feelings about other people. The visible 心 component gives beginners a memorable shape to practise.

components.explanation: 相 sits above 心. Within 相, 木 is on the left and 目 on the right; the lower heart form supports both.

readingNotes: 想 is xiǎng with a third tone. In 想你 (xiǎng nǐ), the first third tone changes to a rising tone in normal speech, while dictionary Pinyin retains the third-tone mark.
usage: 想 means want before an action, think when considering an idea, and miss before a person. 我想喝茶 and 我想你 therefore use the same character with different senses.
writingTip: Keep 相 compact enough to leave space for 心 and its separated dots, and centre the lower hook beneath the upper pair.

exampleSentences.meaning: I would like to drink tea.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 我住在国外的时候，很想念家人。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài guówài de shíhou, hěn xiǎngniàn jiārén.
exampleSentences.meaning: I missed my family when I lived abroad.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 想 adds 心 beneath 相; without the heart component the character and its reading change.

seo.title: 想 (xiǎng) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 想 (xiǎng): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 想 (xiǎng), with 相 above 心. Distinguish wanting to do something, thinking, and missing someone through practical sentences.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 看; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: 看 is useful for reading instructions, watching films, and looking for something. Practise the eye-shaped lower part before comparing its different word senses.

components.explanation: A hand-like upper part extends over 目. The lower eye-shaped box contains two inner horizontals.

readingNotes: Use kàn for looking, watching, or reading in 看书 and 看见. The first-tone reading kān appears in 看守 (kānshǒu, guard) and 看门 (kānmén, watch a door).
usage: 看 can mean read a book, watch a film, or look at something. 看见 emphasises seeing a result, while 看病 means consult a doctor or treat a patient depending on the subject.
writingTip: Leave enough height for 目 beneath the sloping upper part, and keep both inner horizontals visible inside the lower box.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Nǐ kànjiàn wǒ de shǒujī le ma?

exampleSentences.hanzi: 周末我们想一起去看电影。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen xiǎng yìqǐ qù kàn diànyǐng.
exampleSentences.meaning: We would like to see a film together this weekend.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 看 has a hand-like top above 目, while 着 has a different upper set of strokes.

seo.title: 看 (kàn) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 看 (kàn): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 看 (kàn) stroke order and its read, watch, and look meanings. Compare 看 with 看见 and note kān in guarding-related words.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 听; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: Listening is central to a first Chinese lesson. 听 connects that classroom action with useful distinctions between listening and actually hearing a sound.

components.explanation: A small 口 stands beside 斤. The right component has two slanting strokes, a horizontal, and a descending vertical.

readingNotes: 听 is tīng with a level first tone. It remains first tone in 听说 and 听见; the second character carries the changing tone in these compounds.
usage: 听 focuses on listening, while 听见 says that a sound was heard. 听说 can mean hear that something is true, not only listen and speak as two separate actions.
writingTip: Keep 口 narrow and the top slants of 斤 clear, then leave room for the right vertical to descend below its horizontal.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒ tīngjiàn yǒu rén jiào wǒ.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 每天听一点汉语可以帮助你练习听力。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Měitiān tīng yìdiǎn Hànyǔ kěyǐ bāngzhù nǐ liànxí tīnglì.
exampleSentences.meaning: Listening to a little Chinese every day can help you practise listening skills.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 听 has 口 on the left of 斤; 近 combines 斤 with the walking radical 辶.

seo.title: 听 (tīng) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 听 (tīng): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 听 (tīng), with 口 beside 斤. Learn listening versus hearing a result in 听见 and the reported-information use of 听说.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 读; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: 读 links character recognition with reading aloud. Practise it alongside 看 and 写 to describe different learning activities accurately.

components.explanation: The speech radical 讠 is narrow on the left, while 卖 forms the larger right component with a spreading lower finish.

readingNotes: Read 读 as dú in 读书, 阅读, and 读音. A specialist dòu reading occurs in 句读, referring to traditional punctuation or phrasing; it is not used in the beginner examples.
usage: 读 means read and can refer to reading aloud or studying. 看书 often describes reading silently, while 朗读 explicitly means read aloud; 读音 means pronunciation.
writingTip: Keep 讠 narrow and align the levels of 卖 on the right, leaving room for its final spreading strokes.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Zhège zì de dúyīn shì shénme?

exampleSentences.hanzi: 老师请我们大声朗读这篇课文。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Lǎoshī qǐng wǒmen dàshēng lǎngdú zhè piān kèwén.
exampleSentences.meaning: The teacher asked us to read this text aloud.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 读 and 话 share 讠, but 读 has 卖 on the right while 话 has 舌.

seo.title: 读 (dú) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 读 (dú): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 读 (dú), with 讠 beside 卖. Distinguish 读书, 看书, and 朗读, and practise words for pronunciation and reading.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 写; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 写 is the action this tool helps you practise. Learning the cover and lower turns gives beginners a useful word for handwriting and written work.

components.explanation: 冖 forms a shallow cover above a 与-shaped lower part. The cover is distinct from the lower turn and horizontal.

readingNotes: 写 is xiě with a third tone in 写字 and 写作. Before another third tone, such as 写好, the first syllable changes tone in connected speech while the written citation tone stays xiě.
usage: 写 is the action of writing. 写字 focuses on forming written characters, 写作 on composition, and 听写 on writing what is heard; these are related but different tasks.
writingTip: Keep 冖 broad and shallow, then leave enough room under the cover for the lower turn, hook, and separate horizontal.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Qǐng xiě xià nǐ de míngzi.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 每天认真书写几个字，比一次写很多更容易坚持。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Měitiān rènzhēn shūxiě jǐ ge zì, bǐ yí cì xiě hěn duō gèng róngyì jiānchí.
exampleSentences.meaning: Writing a few characters carefully each day is easier to sustain than writing many at once.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 写 adds 冖 over a 与-shaped lower form; omitting the cover changes the character.

seo.title: 写 (xiě) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 写 (xiě): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 写 (xiě) in five strokes. Learn the difference between 写字, 写作, and 听写, with form guidance and printable character practice.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 谢谢; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: 谢谢 is useful from a learner's first conversation. The more detailed shape of 谢 offers a progression from simple speech-radical characters.

components.explanation: The speech radical 讠 stands beside 射. Within 射, 身 is on the left and 寸 on the right, creating a compact three-part arrangement.

readingNotes: 谢 is xiè with a fourth tone. In the common word 谢谢, the second syllable is usually neutral xie in ordinary speech; the careful citation form can retain xièxiè.
usage: 谢谢 is the everyday expression of thanks, while 感谢 is useful in more formal thanks. 谢绝 means politely decline, so 谢 does not express gratitude in every compound.
writingTip: Keep 讠 slim and divide the remaining width between 身 and 寸, ensuring that the small dot in 寸 stays visible.

exampleSentences.meaning: Thank you very much for your help.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 老师耐心地回答了问题，我们都向她道谢。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Lǎoshī nàixīn de huídá le wèntí, wǒmen dōu xiàng tā dàoxiè.
exampleSentences.meaning: The teacher answered patiently, and we all thanked her.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 谢 includes 讠 on the left of 射; dropping it removes the speech radical and changes the word.

seo.title: 谢 (xiè) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 谢 (xiè): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 谢 (xiè) stroke order and neutral xie in 谢谢. Practise everyday thanks, formal 感谢, and the distinct refusal meaning of 谢绝.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 汉语; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: 汉语 names the language learners are practising. 语 connects language names with speaking and grammar vocabulary while reinforcing the speech radical.

components.explanation: The speech radical 讠 occupies the left side and 吾 sits on the right, with 五 above a compact 口.

readingNotes: Use yǔ with a third tone in 汉语, 英语, and 口语. A literary yù reading means tell or inform in certain classical contexts; modern language names here use yǔ.
usage: 语 appears in language names and forms of speech. 汉语 is Chinese, 英语 is English, and 口语 refers to spoken language; 语法 means grammar rather than a particular language.
writingTip: Keep 讠 narrow, centre 五 above the right-hand 口, and avoid stretching that small box into the left radical.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 和朋友用汉语聊天能帮助你提高口语。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Hé péngyou yòng Hànyǔ liáotiān néng bāngzhù nǐ tígāo kǒuyǔ.
exampleSentences.meaning: Chatting with friends in Chinese can help improve your speaking.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 语 and 说 share 讠, but their right components differ: 吾 in 语 and 兑 in 说.

seo.title: 语 (yǔ) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 语 (yǔ): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 语 (yǔ), with 讠 beside 吾. Learn language names, spoken-language vocabulary, and 语法, while distinguishing 语 from 说.
